title: String Secrets
description: Learn how to use Python's text commands to find lengths, capitalize, lower case, or change parts of your text strings!

content.value: Strings aren't just for reading. Python gives us built-in functions to modify and inspect text! Let's look at some cool built-in spells.
To find out how many characters (letters, numbers, and even spaces!) are in a string, we use the `len()` spell.

message = "Hello World"
print(len(message))  # Prints 11 (5 letters + 1 space + 5 letters)
Want to make your text shout? Use `.upper()`! Want to whisper it? Use `.lower()`!

msg = "Coding is Fun!"
print(msg.upper())  # Prints: CODING IS FUN!
print(msg.lower())  # Prints: coding is fun!
If you want to swap a word inside your string, you can use `.replace()`! It takes two arguments: the old word you want to replace, and the new word you want instead.

sentence = "I like apples"
new_sentence = sentence.replace("apples", "cookies")
print(new_sentence)  # Prints: I like cookies

quiz.question: Which function gives you the number of characters in a string?
quiz.explain: `len()` counts the characters in a string. (`length()` isn't a Python function.)

quiz.question: What does 'hello'.upper() return?
quiz.explain: `.upper()` turns every letter UPPERCASE, so 'hello' becomes 'HELLO'.
